newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 29.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - After hours of talks yesterday, the coalition agreed on a stabilisation and revitalisation programme to solve current economic problems. The programme includes measures to cut government spending, freeze the volume of state wages, prepare a slightly surplus budget for 1998 and support the central bank's restrictive policy to slow inflation and growth in the budget deficit.

- The coalition decided yesterday on changes within the cabinet. It will change four ministers. Ivan Pilip will move from the Education Ministry to the Finance Ministry, replacing Ivan Kocarnik. Pilip will be replaced by the Czech ambassador in Germany, Jiri Grusa. Interior Minister Jan Ruml will be replaced by Petr Necas, and Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy will be replaced by the ambassador in Britain, Karel Kuhnl.
- During meetings today with Czech experts, the EU should reach a compromise on the question of the import deposit, which it rejected up to now.
- Beginning today, Komercni Banka is offering two new timed accounts. Deposits tied to the reference rate, which until now were only for six months, can now be deposited for two weeks and one month.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The crown's rate calmed yesterday. Retailers reacted to the cancellation of the fluctuation band by quickly increasing prices, electrical appliances by up to 20 percent, some imported automobiles by 10 percent.
- Most travel agencies want to increase the prices of some trips abroad by five to 10 percent due to the fall of the crown.
- Some domestic drug distributors stopped supplies of foreign medicines to pharmacies in the past few days in reaction to the rate of the crown.

- Yesterday, Union Banka increased interest rates for timed currency accounts. Dollars deposited for one month have interest of four percent, for marks, interest for one month deposits is two percent.
- Transgas, the monopoly gas importer, had net profits last year of 2.756 million crowns with revenue of 35.765 billion crown.

PRAVO - The leader of the opposition Social Democrats, Milos Zeman, criticised the coalition's decisions yesterday, primarily its plan to move Ivan Pilip from the Education Ministry to the Finance Ministry.
- The chairman of the Czech-Moravian federation of labour unions, Richard Falbr, said unions will take a harder line after the announcement of the coalition's programme to save the economy.
- Higher imports of grains make up most of the trade deficit in agricultural commodities. From January until the end of April, grains worth 1.83 billion crowns were imported.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Due to the decline in the crown, Ceska Rafinerska, the largest domestic fuel producer, will increase its sale price of petrol from June 1 by 44 hellers per litre and motor oils by 42 hellers per litre.
- The city of Prague should approve an increase in basic capital for Prvni Mestska Banka from 612 million to 1,224 million crowns today.

- The Institute for Information Theory and Automatisation AV CR presented two new weapons yesterday called Tarantula and Kraken. Tarantula, with a laser locator, will be used for eliminating bomb traps placed in populated places. Kraken is a personal weapon, advantageous for calming demonstrations.
- AGB Media Facts will begin using people metres to measure television viewing from June 1. The project has a five-year budget of more than 300 million crowns.

- According to a survey from the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU), during the first half of this year, import prices increased year-on-year by 10 percent. Exports are predicted to increase by seven percent, year-on-year. The trade deficit is expected to reach 85 billion crowns for the first half.
